stories.title: A total solar eclipse sweeps across mainland Europe for the first time since 1999
stories.what_happened: Totality began around **15:34 GMT** and swept west to east across the path, lasting up to two minutes eighteen seconds at its longest point. An estimated **15 million people**, most of them in Spain, were positioned inside the path of totality, with Iceland catching the eclipse in the late afternoon before the Moon's shadow raced on toward Spain near sunset. The event doubled as a triple sky show: it coincided with the peak of the **Perseid meteor shower** and followed a rare six-planet alignment visible before dawn the same day. Scientists in Spain and Iceland used the brief window of darkness to study the Sun's corona, a layer of the Sun's atmosphere that is normally washed out by direct sunlight and can only be observed properly during totality or with specialized instruments.
key_points: The Moon fully blocked the Sun over **Iceland, Greenland and northern Spain** — the first total eclipse seen from mainland Europe in **27 years**.
Up to **15 million people**, mostly in Spain, sat inside the narrow 'path of totality' where the sky went dark in daytime.
Totality lasted up to **2 minutes 18 seconds** at its longest point along the path.
The eclipse coincided with the peak of the **Perseid meteor shower** and a rare pre-dawn alignment of six planets.
Scientists used the brief darkness to study the Sun's **corona**, its outer atmosphere that's normally invisible in daylight.

depth.background: A total solar eclipse happens when the Moon passes directly between the Earth and the Sun, and its shadow is small enough that only a narrow strip of the planet — the 'path of totality' — experiences full darkness. Because the Moon's shadow is only about 100-160 km wide, most eclipses cross oceans or sparsely populated land; this is the **first one to sweep across mainland Europe since 1999**, and the first ever recorded from the Iberian Peninsula in over a century. The path today ran from Siberian Russia through Greenland and Iceland before reaching northern Spain and Portugal just before sunset.

stories.title: Severe Tropical Storm Chan-hom makes Japan's first-ever recorded typhoon landfall in Ibaraki, disrupting Tokyo
stories.what_happened: Severe Tropical Storm Chan-hom, designated **Typhoon No. 15** by Japan, made landfall in **Ibaraki Prefecture** near Tokyo at around **8:00 p.m. local time** on Tuesday, August 11. The Japan Meteorological Agency confirmed this is the **first typhoon landfall on record in Ibaraki since 1951**. The storm had a central pressure of **980 hectopascals**, sustained winds of **25 meters per second**, and gusts up to **35 meters per second**. Authorities warned of violent winds, high waves, and heavy rain across the Kanto and Tohoku regions, with intense rain expected to continue into August 12. The storm disrupted the Obon holiday travel rush: **ANA cancelled 58 flights** out of Haneda and Narita, **JAL cancelled four**, and JR East suspended parts of its Joban rail line.
key_points: Chan-hom, Japan's **Typhoon No. 15**, made landfall in **Ibaraki Prefecture** near Tokyo on Tuesday night.
It's the **first typhoon landfall recorded in Ibaraki** since Japan began keeping records in **1951**.
The storm carried a central pressure of **980 hectopascals** and gusts up to **35 meters per second**.
**ANA cancelled 58 flights** and JAL cancelled four, disrupting the Obon holiday travel rush.
Japan's weather agency warned of violent winds, high waves, and heavy rain through **August 12**.

depth.background: Japan sits in one of the world's most typhoon-prone regions, and its meteorological agency has tracked storm landfalls in detail since 1951 — one of the most complete disaster records anywhere. The Kanto region, which includes Tokyo and Ibaraki, usually sees typhoons make landfall further south or pass offshore, so a direct hit on Ibaraki itself is statistically unusual. The storm arrived during Japan's mid-August **Obon** holiday, one of the country's busiest travel periods, when millions return to hometowns to honor ancestors.

stories.title: India warns China that the Arunachal Pradesh border 'will define' ties, after unverified reports of troop activity
stories.what_happened: Unverified reports from local residents claimed Chinese troops had entered areas near Pukar La and Ollo, in the Upper Subansiri region of Arunachal Pradesh. India's Ministry of External Affairs responded on August 11 by reasserting that Arunachal Pradesh is 'an integral part of India' and warning that the state of the border 'will define' the broader bilateral relationship — without directly confirming or denying the specific troop-movement claims. The statement came five days after the two countries held their 36th round of Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination (WMCC) talks in New Delhi on August 6. Notably, Arunachal Pradesh's Chief Minister Pema Khandu publicly downplayed the reports even as the central government's language stayed firm, and the Indian Army itself has not confirmed the claims.
key_points: Local residents reported **Chinese troops** entering areas near **Pukar La and Ollo** in Arunachal Pradesh's Upper Subansiri region — but this is **not yet confirmed** by the Indian Army.
India's Ministry of External Affairs said on **August 11** that the state of the border 'will define' the wider India-China relationship.
Arunachal Pradesh's own Chief Minister, **Pema Khandu**, publicly downplayed the reports — a rare public gap between state and central government messaging.
It follows the **36th round** of India-China border talks (the WMCC) held in New Delhi on **August 6**.

depth.background: India and China share a long, disputed border known as the **Line of Actual Control (LAC)**, including in Arunachal Pradesh, which China claims in its entirety as 'South Tibet' while India administers it as a full state. Relations have been cautiously stabilizing since a deadly 2020 clash in Galwan Valley, including a resumption of high-level border talks — but any reported troop movement near the LAC has historically been enough to reignite tension quickly, given how sensitive and heavily militarized the frontier is on both sides.

stories.title: LEAP India's ₹2,480-crore IPO closes 2.84x subscribed, on track to list August 14
stories.what_happened: LEAP India's ₹2,480-crore initial public offering closed for bidding on Tuesday, its final day, having been subscribed **2.84 times** overall. The **qualified institutional buyer (QIB)** portion — typically large funds and banks — was subscribed 4.62 times, the non-institutional (high-net-worth individual) portion 4.74 times, while the retail investor quota was just barely covered at 1.01 times. In total, bids came in for **32.68 crore shares** against roughly 11.5 crore shares on offer. The company will finalize share allotments on August 12, with trading set to begin on the NSE and BSE on **August 14**.
key_points: LEAP India's **₹2,480-crore IPO** closed on its final day, subscribed **2.84 times overall**.
Qualified institutional buyers bid **4.62x** their quota and non-institutional investors **4.74x**, while retail just crossed 1x.
Bids came in for **32.68 crore shares** against 11.5 crore on offer.
Allotment is due **August 12**, with shares set to debut on the **NSE and BSE on August 14**.
It's one of **five IPOs** open this week, part of a busy August for India's primary market.

depth.background: LEAP India is a pallet-pooling and industrial-rental company — it supplies and manages reusable pallets and crates that manufacturers and retailers use to move goods through supply chains, a niche but growing logistics-infrastructure business in India. Indian IPO activity has been especially heavy this week, with LEAP India, Technocraft Ventures, Molbio Diagnostics, Dhoot Transmission, and Milky Mist Dairy all raising money from investors simultaneously — a sign of strong risk appetite in India's primary market even as broader indices have been choppy on oil-price worries.

stories.title: Government summons Air India's CEO over mid-air drop that injured 20+, as the pilot fails a second drug test
stories.what_happened: On August 4, Air India flight AI2379, an Airbus A320 flying from Phuket to Delhi carrying 137 passengers (including 3 infants) and 8 crew, suffered a sudden altitude drop of roughly 300 feet mid-flight, injuring an estimated **20 to 24 people** onboard. On August 11, the Ministry of Civil Aviation and the DGCA summoned Air India's outgoing CEO **Campbell Wilson** to explain the airline's response, with officials citing the 'fragile' state of public confidence in the wake of the AI171 crash last year. Separately, the pilot-in-command's second post-flight drug test came back as a **confirmatory positive** for marijuana, adding a conduct dimension to what began as a technical incident. India's Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) has classified the event as 'serious', a category that brought in France's BEA (Bureau d'Enquêtes et d'Analyses) and Airbus itself to assist the probe.
key_points: The DGCA summoned outgoing CEO **Campbell Wilson** after flight AI2379 from Phuket suffered a sudden **300-foot** altitude drop on **August 4**, injuring around **20-24** people.
The pilot-in-command's second post-flight test came back **positive for marijuana**, turning a technical scare into a conduct scandal too.
Investigators classified the incident as **'serious'**, pulling in France's air-accident bureau (BEA) and Airbus for support.
It comes just over a year after the **AI171** crash, which officials say has left public confidence in Air India 'fragile'.

depth.background: Air India has been under Tata Group ownership since 2022, in the middle of a multi-year turnaround meant to modernize a once state-run airline with an aging safety reputation. That turnaround was already under intense scrutiny after the **AI171** crash last year, one of India's deadliest aviation disasters in decades. The **DGCA** (Directorate General of Civil Aviation) is India's aviation safety regulator, with the power to summon airline executives and ground crew over safety lapses.

stories.title: Former Australia star Moises Henriques to captain Portugal in T20 World Cup qualifiers
stories.what_happened: Henriques was named captain of Portugal's 14-player squad for the ICC T20 World Cup Europe Sub-Regional Qualifier C, being held in Finland from August 14 to 20, 2026. Portugal are grouped alongside Israel, Germany, Greece and the Czech Republic; the group winner advances toward a European regional final alongside Scotland, Jersey and Denmark, with the top finishers from that stage progressing toward the global qualifying pathway for the 2028 T20 World Cup in Australia and New Zealand. It marks Portugal's push to reach a T20 World Cup for the first time in the country's history. The squad also includes players such as Craig Cachopa, Edward Fleming and wicketkeeper Dhavalkumar Norotam.
key_points: **Moises Henriques**, 39, who retired from Australian domestic cricket last month, will captain **Portugal's** 14-player squad.
The ICC T20 World Cup **Europe Sub-Regional Qualifier C** runs in Finland from **August 14-20**.
Portugal are grouped with **Israel, Germany, Greece and the Czech Republic**; the group winner advances toward a European regional final.
It's part of Portugal's bid to reach a **T20 World Cup for the first time ever**.

depth.background: Cricket's global qualifying system lets 'associate' nations — countries without full Test-playing status — work their way toward major ICC tournaments through regional qualifiers. Henriques, born in Madeira, Portugal, played for Australia internationally and had a long IPL career including with Sunrisers Hyderabad; his Portuguese heritage makes him eligible to represent Portugal, joining a broader trend of established professionals turning out for smaller cricketing nations.

stories.title: Ferrari poaches two chassis engineers from Mercedes and Aston Martin to build its 2027 car
stories.what_happened: Ferrari has recruited two engineers from rival teams to reinforce its chassis department. Luciano Nicomede, who had spent over four years at Mercedes' Brackley factory as a composite design engineer, announced the move himself on LinkedIn. Separately, Carlos Sánchez Martínez, a chassis stress-engineering specialist who had been at Aston Martin since its Racing Point days in 2019, started at Ferrari's Maranello base in July 2026. Both now sit under chassis chief Fabio Montecchi, who reports to technical director Loïc Serra, and are reportedly already shaping the characteristics of Ferrari's 2027 monocoque — the carbon-fibre structural tub at the heart of the car.
key_points: **Luciano Nicomede**, a composite design engineer, left Mercedes after **four years** to join Ferrari's chassis team.
**Carlos Sánchez Martínez**, a stress-engineering specialist, moved over from **Aston Martin**, where he'd been since the team was Racing Point back in 2019.
Both now report to chassis chief **Fabio Montecchi** under technical director **Loïc Serra**, and are already working on Ferrari's **2027 monocoque**.
It signals Ferrari stacking specialist talent ahead of F1's next major rules reset in **2027**.

depth.background: In Formula 1, a team's chassis department — the engineers who design the car's structural 'tub' — is one of the most specialized and closely-guarded parts of the operation, and hiring away a rival's specialists is a common early signal of how seriously a team is preparing for a coming regulation change. F1 is heading into a major new technical ruleset in 2027, meaning every top team is now quietly building its next-generation car well ahead of the season it will actually race.

stories.title: Milky Mist's ₹1,553-crore IPO opens today, the largest ever by an Indian dairy company
stories.what_happened: Milky Mist Dairy Food's IPO opened for subscription today, August 11, giving investors a three-day window to bid for shares before the issue closes on **August 13**. The company has fixed a price band of **₹133 to ₹140** per share, with a lot size of 107 shares meaning a retail investor needs roughly **₹14,980** at the top end to apply for a single lot. The **₹1,553-crore** offering combines a fresh issue of 10.20 crore shares worth up to ₹1,428 crore — money that goes to the company itself — with an offer for sale of 89.28 lakh shares worth up to ₹125 crore, where existing shareholders sell down their stake. The tentative allotment date is August 14, with refunds and share credits by August 17, and listing on the NSE targeted for **August 18**.
key_points: Milky Mist Dairy Food's **₹1,553-crore IPO** opened for subscription today, closing **August 13**.
The price band is set at **₹133-₹140 per share**, with a lot size of **107 shares**.
A retail investor needs about **₹14,980** to bid for one lot at the top of the price band.
It combines a **₹1,428-crore fresh issue** with a **₹125-crore offer for sale**.
Shares are expected to list on the **NSE on August 18**.

depth.background: An **IPO (Initial Public Offering)** is when a private company sells shares to the public for the first time, raising money while letting existing owners and early investors cash out part of their stake. Milky Mist is a packaged dairy products company, and this listing is being marketed as the **largest IPO ever by an Indian dairy company**, arriving in the middle of an unusually busy week for India's primary market, which is seeing nine IPOs collectively target nearly ₹7,700 crore.

stories.title: Romania destroys two Russian-made drones found drifting near its biggest Black Sea gas project
stories.what_happened: Romanian army divers carried out a controlled detonation of **two Gerbera-type drones** found floating, not flying, in the Black Sea on August 11, Defence Minister Radu Miruță said. They were spotted by a vessel working in the area about **90 nautical miles from Constanța**, near the Neptun Deep gas project. Gerbera drones are a low-cost Russian decoy/strike drone based on Iran's Shahed design, often used alongside real attack drones to overwhelm air defenses. The operation caused no injuries or damage. Ukraine said the drones were not its own, effectively pointing to Russia as the source, though Romanian officials stopped short of formally attributing them.
key_points: Romanian navy divers destroyed **two Gerbera-type drones** found adrift in the Black Sea on August 11.
The drones were spotted roughly **90 nautical miles** off the port of Constanța, near the **Neptun Deep** gas field.
Gerbera drones are a **cheap, Russian-made decoy/attack drone**, modeled on Iran's Shahed design.
Ukraine confirmed the drones were **not its own** — leaving Russia as the likely source, though Romania hasn't formally assigned blame.
**Neptun Deep** is due to come online in 2027 and would make Romania the **EU's largest gas producer**.

depth.background: Romania is a **NATO** member and sits on the Black Sea directly across from Ukraine's Odesa region, where Russian and Ukrainian drone debris has washed up repeatedly since the war began. **Neptun Deep**, jointly owned by Austria's OMV Petrom and Romania's state gas firm Romgaz, is the country's biggest energy investment in decades — a deep-water gas field expected to sharply cut Romania's, and the region's, reliance on imported gas once it starts producing in 2027. Stray war debris drifting into NATO waters has become a recurring flashpoint, occasionally triggering fighter-jet scrambles.

stories.title: Isack Hadjar opens up on the 'culture shock' of his mid-season promotion to partner Verstappen at Red Bull
stories.what_happened: In new comments, Hadjar admitted he suffered a 'culture shock' moving from Racing Bulls, which he described as a more family-like, Italian-flavoured operation, to Red Bull's British-run senior team, despite both falling under the same parent energy-drink company. He said his years in Red Bull's junior program — including driving Verstappen's own car during a practice session at the 2024 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix — made the transition considerably less jarring than a standard move between rival constructors would have been. Hadjar also noted his working relationship with race engineer Richard 'Woody' Wood dates back three years, to those same early junior outings.
key_points: **Isack Hadjar** described switching from Racing Bulls' more 'family, Italian' environment to Red Bull's British operation as a genuine **culture shock**.
He was promoted to partner **Max Verstappen** at Red Bull after a strong rookie season in 2025.

Hadjar says his history in Red Bull's junior program — including driving Verstappen's car during practice at the **2024 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix** — made the move less jarring than a typical switch between rival teams.
His working relationship with race engineer **'Woody' (Richard Wood)** actually began three years ago during those early outings.

depth.background: Red Bull operates a junior driver 'feeder' system, historically running its sister team (now called Racing Bulls) as a proving ground before promoting drivers to the main Red Bull squad. Hadjar's promotion this season adds fresh stakes given the already-reported activation of Verstappen's Red Bull exit clause, which makes the stability of his new teammate more significant to the team's future.

stories.title: Amnesty International warns Afghanistan's cricket series in Ireland risks becoming 'Taliban propaganda'
stories.what_happened: With Ireland hosting Afghanistan for a five-match men's ODI series (two games at Bready, three at Belfast's Stormont, with Stormont fixtures on August 10, 12 and 15), Cricket Ireland has arranged security plans with the Police Service of Northern Ireland in anticipation of demonstrations. Amnesty International spokesperson Felix Jakens told BBC Sport that 'the Taliban will look to harness this series for propaganda purposes,' comparing the dynamic to other regimes using sport to 'launder their image.' Jakens called on Cricket Ireland and the ICC to keep the plight of Afghan women in focus throughout the series and to fully respect the right to peaceful protest around the matches.
key_points: Cricket Ireland has security plans in place with police as it hosts Afghanistan for a **five-match ODI series**, with fixtures at Bready and Belfast's Stormont.
Amnesty International's **Felix Jakens** said the Taliban 'will look to harness this series for propaganda purposes', comparing it to other regimes using sport to launder their image.
The controversy centers on the Taliban's near-total ban on **women's sport, education and public life** since taking power in 2021.
Amnesty is calling on Cricket Ireland and the **ICC** to keep Afghan women's exclusion in focus while still honouring the right to peaceful protest.

depth.background: Afghanistan's men's cricket team continues to compete internationally even though the Taliban government has banned women and girls from playing sport, attending school past a certain age, and taking part in most public life since retaking power in 2021. This tension has repeatedly put other cricket boards — including Australia and England — under pressure over whether continuing to play Afghanistan implicitly legitimizes the Taliban, or whether keeping the team engaged is the better way to keep pressure on the regime.

stories.title: Alpine bets its 'critical' Zandvoort upgrade on saving its shot at 5th place
stories.what_happened: Alpine driver Pierre Gasly said the team's planned upgrade package for the Dutch Grand Prix at Zandvoort — including **'some pretty big new aero parts'** — is critical to keeping Alpine's hopes of finishing 5th in the constructors' championship alive this season. The comments came as Alpine, along with rivals like McLaren and Aston Martin, prepares to introduce significant new parts once the F1 summer break ends and the season resumes at Zandvoort on **August 21-23**. Gasly's remarks underline how much competitive pressure is riding on a single upgrade package landing correctly.
key_points: Alpine driver **Pierre Gasly** says a **big aero upgrade** due at the Dutch Grand Prix is **'critical'** for the team's 2026 hopes.
Alpine is fighting to hold onto **5th place** in the constructors' championship.
The upgrade lands at **Zandvoort (August 21-23)**, right after F1's summer break.
It follows a pattern this season of teams saving their **biggest updates** for the post-break run of races.
Rivals **McLaren** and **Aston Martin** are also pushing new parts around the same window, raising the stakes for Alpine.

depth.background: Formula 1 teams get a fixed budget each season under the **cost cap**, so most save their biggest aerodynamic upgrades for a few key races rather than spreading small tweaks all year. The August summer shutdown is a natural moment for that: teams use the forced downtime to finish parts in the factory, then bring them out together at the next race. Alpine has struggled in the midfield this year and is locked in a tight fight for 5th in the constructors' standings, a position worth significant prize money.

stories.title: Ukrainian drones set Russian oil refineries and a warehouse ablaze up to 6,500km from the front line
stories.what_happened: Overnight into August 11, Ukrainian drones struck a Wildberries logistics hub in Russia's Voronezh region, killing a **49-year-old man** hit by falling drone debris and setting fire to roughly 36,000 square metres of warehouse space. Ukraine's military separately confirmed strikes on the **Orsknefteorgsintez oil refinery** in Orenburg region, hitting a primary refining unit there, some 1,500 km from the Ukrainian border. Further east, a fire broke out at a **Rosneft refinery in Komsomolsk-on-Amur**, in Russia's Far East — over 6,500 km from Ukraine — though the exact cause and any Ukrainian link there remains unconfirmed. The strikes came the same week Russia hit Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region with North Korean-made ballistic missiles.
key_points: Ukrainian drones hit a Rosneft refinery in **Komsomolsk-on-Amur**, in Russia's Far East — roughly **6,500 km** from Ukraine.
A strike on a **Wildberries** logistics hub in Voronezh killed **one person** and tore through **36,000 square metres** of warehouse space.
Ukraine's military also confirmed hitting the **Orsknefteorgsintez refinery** in Orenburg region, about **1,500 km** from the border.
It's the latest round in Ukraine's campaign to squeeze Russia's fuel supply and its biggest e-commerce logistics network.

depth.background: Since 2025, Ukraine has run a sustained long-range drone campaign against Russian oil refineries — the plants that turn crude oil into usable fuel — aiming to choke off Russia's ability to fuel its military and economy, and it has triggered real domestic fuel shortages in Russia before. Wildberries, the target hit in Voronezh, is **Russia's largest online retailer** (similar in scale to Amazon in the US), and its warehouses have increasingly become targets as Ukraine broadens strikes to logistics infrastructure, not just energy sites.

stories.title: Sensex and Nifty slide as oil prices jump on fading hopes for a Strait of Hormuz deal
stories.what_happened: India's benchmark indices opened weak on Tuesday and extended losses through the morning: by around 11am IST, the **Nifty50 was down 112.9 points (0.46%)** at 24,470.90, and the **Sensex had fallen 362.57 points (0.46%)** to 78,177.87. The trigger is oil — **Brent crude jumped roughly 5% to settle near $87.72 a barrel** as hopes dimmed that the US and Iran will strike a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. President Trump told Axios the US is only **'semi-negotiating'** with Iran, undercutting his own earlier claims that talks were serious, while Iran has rejected direct talks and is demanding an end to the US naval blockade, sanctions relief, and compensation for war damage before it reopens shipping. Top losers on the Nifty50 included **InterGlobe Aviation, Bajaj Finance and Shriram Finance** — aviation and financing names especially sensitive to fuel and funding costs.
key_points: Nifty50 down **112.9 points (0.46%)** to 24,470.90, Sensex down **362.57 points** by mid-morning
Trigger: Brent crude jumped roughly **5% to $87.72/barrel** on fading Hormuz-deal hopes
Trump told Axios the US is only **'semi-negotiating'** with Iran, undercutting earlier talk of real progress
Top losers included **InterGlobe Aviation, Bajaj Finance, Shriram Finance** — fuel- and funding-cost sensitive names
Comes right after the **RBI defended the rupee** near 95.4/dollar over the weekend

depth.background: India imports over **80% of the crude oil** it consumes, so a sustained oil-price jump hits the economy on multiple fronts: it widens the trade deficit, pressures the rupee, and pushes up domestic fuel and transport costs that can feed into inflation. The **Strait of Hormuz** — the narrow shipping lane roughly a fifth of the world's oil passes through — has been a flashpoint for months amid the wider US-Israel-Iran standoff. The RBI had already stepped in over the weekend to defend the rupee as it neared the psychologically important 95.4-to-the-dollar level.

thread.previously: We reported the RBI stepping in to defend the rupee as rising oil prices threatened to push it past 95.4 to the dollar, while the Sensex opened flat around 24,500 as strong global cues offset a quiet start to the week.
thread.changed: That pressure has turned into an outright selloff: Brent crude jumped roughly 5% as hopes for a US-Iran deal on reopening the Strait of Hormuz faded, and both the Sensex and Nifty fell over 0.4% by mid-morning Tuesday.

stories.title: Trump signals a pivot to economic pressure on Iran as the Strait of Hormuz standoff grinds past five months
stories.what_happened: President Trump told Axios he is **'low keying it'** and only 'semi-negotiating' with Iran, saying the US will let economic pressure — not further military strikes — do the work of forcing Tehran back to the table. He pointed to Iran's **'huge inflation'** and the fact that, in his telling, Iran can no longer pay its own troops, as evidence the strategy is succeeding. US Central Command said American forces had redirected **55 commercial vessels** headed toward Hormuz as of Sunday, up sharply from 35 as of August 2, and that US forces have also disabled two ships and boarded two others to enforce compliance. The Treasury separately announced its **eighth Iran sanctions package of 2026**, targeting the country's alleged shadow-banking system, which it says helps Iran evade existing sanctions. Iran, meanwhile, has issued a new list of conditions Washington must meet before it will allow normal shipping through the Strait again.
key_points: Trump told Axios he is **'low keying it'** with Iran, betting that sanctions and a naval blockade squeeze Tehran instead of further US strikes.
US Central Command says it has redirected **55 commercial vessels** as of Sunday, up from 35 on August 2, as the blockade tightens.
The Treasury issued its **eighth Iran-related sanctions round of 2026**, targeting what it calls Iran's 'shadow banking' network.
Trump cited Iran's **soaring inflation** and inability to pay its own troops as evidence the pressure campaign is working.
Iran has issued a fresh list of demands before it will reopen the Strait of Hormuz, keeping the crisis in its **sixth month**.

depth.background: The Strait of Hormuz is a narrow shipping lane between Iran and Oman through which roughly a fifth of the world's oil passes; Iran has kept it effectively closed for over five months amid its standoff with the US, after a missile strike hit a UAE oil tanker there and Iran's security council declared the strait would stay shut until Washington 'corrects its behavior.' Trump had weighed further military action but is now emphasizing that a US naval blockade is already straining Iran's economy. This is part of a broader 'maximum pressure' sanctions campaign the Treasury has run against Iran for most of 2026.

thread.previously: We reported Iran's security council hardening its stance and declaring the Strait would stay shut until the US 'corrects its behavior,' just as a shipping deal had appeared close.
thread.changed: Trump is now publicly shifting strategy — away from the threat of military action and toward sanctions and a naval blockade — while Iran has issued fresh demands, showing the standoff deepening rather than resolving.

stories.title: Russia hits Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia with North Korean-made ballistic missiles, killing at least six
stories.what_happened: Russian forces launched a wave of ballistic missiles and drones at Ukraine overnight into Tuesday, August 11. In **Zaporizhzhia**, regional head Ivan Fedorov said the attack killed **six people**, injured **19**, and damaged four apartment buildings along with several non-residential buildings. President **Volodymyr Zelenskyy** said the ballistic missiles used in the strike were supplied by **North Korea**, part of a deepening military partnership between Moscow and Pyongyang. A separate missile struck near a children's hospital in Kyiv's Shevchenkivskyi district — no one was hurt there — while another strike sparked a warehouse fire that injured one person. In the central Dnipropetrovsk region, Russian drones and artillery killed three more people, including a **15-year-old boy**.
key_points: Russian forces killed at least **six people** and wounded **19** in overnight strikes on Zaporizhzhia.
President Zelenskyy says the ballistic missiles used were **supplied by North Korea**.
A separate strike hit Kyiv, sparking fires near a **children's hospital**.
**Three more people**, including a 15-year-old, died in a drone-and-artillery strike on Dnipropetrovsk.
The attack follows Kyiv's own warning that Russia is scaling up toward **200-missile mass strikes**.

depth.background: Russia has spent the summer of 2026 escalating long-range strikes on Ukrainian cities even as diplomatic efforts to end the war continue on and off. North Korea has quietly become one of Russia's most important wartime partners, supplying artillery shells and troops, and — increasingly — ballistic missile technology, in exchange for money, food, and military know-how Pyongyang badly needs. Zaporizhzhia, a frontline industrial city partly occupied by Russia since 2022, is hit regularly because of its proximity to the front line and its power infrastructure.

thread.previously: Ukraine's drone forces commander warned Russia was building toward firing roughly 200 ballistic missiles in a single combined strike — nearly triple the scale of its largest attacks so far in 2026 — and cited it as a case for hitting Russian missile factories directly.
thread.changed: That warning was followed within a day by an actual strike using North Korean-supplied ballistic missiles on Zaporizhzhia, confirming Russia is both expanding its missile supply chain and actively using the new capability.

stories.title: Barbados Tridents edge Jamaica Kingsmen by 5 runs in tight CPL opener at Sabina Park
stories.what_happened: Barbados Tridents beat hosts Jamaica Kingsmen by **5 runs** in the 4th match of the 2026 Caribbean Premier League at **Sabina Park, Kingston**, on **August 11**. Batting first, the Tridents posted **206/3** from their 20 overs, built around a strong middle-overs platform. Chasing 207 to win, Jamaica Kingsmen fought hard but finished on **201/9**, falling **5 runs** short despite a late push. Fast bowler **Daniel Sams** was the difference-maker with the ball, taking **4 wickets for 20 runs** to restrict Jamaica's chase, and was named Player of the Match.
key_points: Barbados Tridents posted **206/3** and held on to beat hosts Jamaica Kingsmen by **5 runs** in Kingston.
Jamaica Kingsmen fell just short, finishing on **201/9** from their 20 overs.
Fast bowler **Daniel Sams** was named Player of the Match for figures of **4/20**.
It's the Tridents' first outing under their restored name, after the Barbados franchise reverted from "Royals" back to **Barbados Tridents** for the 2026 CPL season.

depth.background: The **Caribbean Premier League (CPL)** is the Caribbean's top T20 franchise tournament, running since 2013 and featuring six regional teams stocked with international stars during the Northern Hemisphere's cricket off-season. Barbados's team has changed names before — it was the Tridents in the league's early years before being rebranded the Royals — and the CPL confirmed the **Tridents** name was restored for 2026. Jamaica's franchise, meanwhile, enters this season under a new **Kingsmen** identity, and both teams are opening their campaigns in a tournament where net run rate often decides who reaches the playoffs.

stories.title: Colombia's earthquake death toll surges past 220 as new president says 5,000 homes destroyed
stories.what_happened: The death toll from Sunday's magnitude-7.4 earthquake in western Colombia has climbed to at least **224**, according to a CNN tally, up from roughly 160 a day earlier as rescuers push into harder-to-reach areas. President De La Espriella said in a national briefing that **700 people were injured** and an estimated **5,000 homes** were damaged or destroyed. First responders pulled a woman alive from the rubble of a collapsed building in Cali nearly **30 hours** after the quake hit, one of several dramatic rescues that have kept hope alive even as the toll rises. Colombia's Geological Service has logged more than 70 aftershocks since the main quake, complicating rescue work and unnerving residents already living outdoors. Seven airports have suspended operations and hospitals, roads, aqueducts, power and telecoms remain disrupted across the hardest-hit cities, all of which remain under the country's highest-level red alert.
key_points: Confirmed deaths have risen to at least **224**, up from ~160 a day earlier, as rescue teams reach more remote towns.
President **Abelardo De La Espriella**, newly inaugurated, says **700 people** were injured and an estimated **5,000 homes** damaged or destroyed.
A woman was pulled alive from a collapsed building in **Cali** almost **30 hours** after the quake struck.
Colombia's Geological Service has recorded more than **70 aftershocks** since the magnitude-7.4 quake.
**Seven airports** remain shut and hospitals, roads and power are disrupted across the hardest-hit region.

depth.background: A magnitude-7.4 earthquake struck western Colombia on Sunday, with the epicenter near San Jose del Palmar, flattening buildings across Pereira, Cali, Quibdo, Manizales and Armenia. All five cities remain under Colombia's highest disaster classification, **'red alert.'** Colombia sits atop the Pacific 'Ring of Fire,' where the Nazca oceanic plate grinds beneath South America, making it one of the most earthquake-prone countries on the continent. The disaster is one of the first major tests for **President Abelardo De La Espriella**, who was only recently inaugurated.

stories.title: Israel and Venezuela restore consular ties after a 17-year diplomatic freeze
stories.what_happened: Israel and Venezuela announced on **Tuesday, August 11** that they had agreed to **renew consular relations** after 17 years without formal ties. The agreement, reached after weeks of talks between Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar and Venezuelan Foreign Minister Félix Plasencia, establishes a **coordination mechanism** that will let both countries provide consular services — passports, documentation, and citizen assistance — to their nationals. It stops short of restoring **full diplomatic relations** (embassies and ambassadors), but it is the first official, on-the-record cooperation channel between the two governments since 2009. The thaw follows Israel sending an **aid and disaster-response delegation** to Venezuela in June after twin earthquakes killed thousands, and comes months after the **US toppled Maduro** in a January raid.
key_points: Israel and Venezuela agreed to **renew consular relations**, 17 years after Venezuela cut ties over Gaza.
The deal creates a **coordination mechanism** for consular services — short of full diplomatic relations.
It follows Israel sending an **aid and disaster-response team** to Venezuela after June's twin earthquakes.
It also follows the **US toppling of Nicolás Maduro** in a January 2026 military raid, with interim leader **Delcy Rodríguez** now under heavy pressure from Washington.
Talks were led by Israeli Foreign Minister **Gideon Saar** and Venezuelan counterpart **Félix Plasencia**.

depth.background: Venezuela severed relations with Israel **17 years ago**, under Hugo Chávez, in protest of Israeli military operations in the Gaza Strip — part of a broader anti-US, anti-Israel foreign policy stance that Chávez and later Nicolás Maduro maintained for nearly two decades. That changed dramatically in **January 2026**, when a US military raid toppled Maduro's government; interim president **Delcy Rodríguez** now runs the country under sustained pressure from President Trump to realign Venezuela's foreign policy with Washington's interests, including its energy and diplomatic priorities.

stories.title: Google's Gemini app crosses 1 billion monthly users, closing in on ChatGPT
stories.what_happened: Pichai said on **August 11** that the standalone Gemini app has surpassed **1 billion monthly active users**, calling it one of the company's **fastest-growing products** and the **14th Google product** to hit that scale (alongside Search, Gmail, Maps, YouTube and others). The growth curve has been steep: Gemini had roughly **400 million** monthly users in May 2025, **900 million** a year later, and **950 million** by its most recent quarterly earnings call before crossing the billion mark now. Google also said **daily active users have tripled** over the past year, suggesting people aren't just trying Gemini once but returning to it regularly. The milestone lands just weeks after ChatGPT itself crossed 1 billion monthly users, effectively pulling the two biggest consumer AI products into a **dead heat on raw reach**, even though usage intensity and revenue between them can still differ sharply.
key_points: Google CEO **Sundar Pichai** announced Gemini has passed **1 billion monthly active users**.
It is the **14th Google product** ever to reach the 1-billion-user mark.
Users have **more than doubled in about a year** — Gemini had **400 million** users in May 2025.
Daily active users have **tripled over the past year**, a faster growth rate than the monthly figure alone shows.
The milestone puts Gemini roughly level with **OpenAI's ChatGPT**, which crossed 1 billion monthly users in June 2026.

depth.background: For most of the generative-AI boom that started in late 2022, **ChatGPT** was the runaway leader in consumer AI apps, with Google's Gemini (and its earlier Bard branding) playing catch-up. Google's advantage has always been distribution: Gemini is built into **Android phones, Search, Gmail, and Workspace**, giving it a shortcut to huge user numbers that a standalone app like ChatGPT doesn't have. Over the past 18 months Google has leaned harder into that advantage, pushing Gemini prompts and summaries directly into products **billions of people already use daily**.

stories.title: Max Verstappen's Red Bull exit clause activates, making him F1's biggest free agent
stories.what_happened: Reports on **August 11** confirmed that Max Verstappen is now, in practical terms, a **free agent**: his Red Bull contract's exit clause — triggered by his position outside the **top two** in the drivers' standings when the season entered its summer break — is now active, meaning he can negotiate with rival teams without breaching his contract. Verstappen currently sits behind championship leader **Kimi Antonelli** and has been unable to close the gap as Red Bull's **RB22** has lagged rivals. **Mercedes and McLaren**, the two strongest teams this season, are seen as the most realistic destinations if he decides to leave. It follows Wednesday's news that F1 commercial boss **Stefano Domenicali** had held 'constructive' talks with Verstappen about staying in the sport beyond 2026 — talks that now look more like an attempt to keep him at Red Bull specifically, or in F1 at all, rather than assuming his loyalty.
key_points: Verstappen's **Red Bull contract runs to 2028**, but contains an **exit clause tied to championship position**.
The clause **activated on August 11** because he was outside the **top two** in the standings entering the summer break.
**Mercedes and McLaren** are named as the teams best placed to make a move, given their current competitiveness.
Verstappen has **four F1 world titles** and is widely rated the best driver on the current grid.
Red Bull is currently **fourth in the constructors' standings**, over 200 points behind leaders Mercedes.

depth.background: Modern F1 driver contracts increasingly include **performance-linked exit or release clauses**, which let a top driver leave a struggling team without penalty if the car isn't competitive enough — protecting the driver's title chances from being tied to a team's bad car. Verstappen has won **four consecutive world championships** with Red Bull (2021–2024) but the team has struggled to adapt to F1's new 2026 technical rules, with its **RB22 car** reportedly regarded internally as underperforming. Speculation about Verstappen's future has simmered for much of the season as Red Bull's competitiveness has slipped.

thread.previously: Yesterday, F1 commercial boss Stefano Domenicali said he'd held 'constructive' talks with Verstappen about the four-time champion staying in the sport beyond 2026, amid swirling questions about his future.
thread.changed: Today it emerged the situation is more urgent than 'talks about staying': Verstappen's contract, which runs through 2028, contains a **performance exit clause** that has now formally activated because he entered the summer break outside the top two in the standings — making him a free agent other teams can legally approach.

stories.title: Wall Street slips from record highs as Brazil's cooling inflation reopens the door to a rate cut, gold jumps
stories.what_happened: Data released this week showed Brazil's **IPCA inflation index rose just 0.03% month-on-month in July**, cooling the annual rate to **4.4%**, down from 4.6% in June and matching economist forecasts. Food inflation, a key driver of the recent overshoot, **eased for a second straight month to 3.4%** year-on-year. The reading put headline inflation back within the central bank's target band for the first time in two months, and analysts said it **opens room for a 25-basis-point cut** at the bank's September meeting. Against that backdrop, US stocks were mixed: the **S&P 500 dipped 0.06% to 7,753**, a small pullback from recent record levels, while the **dollar index rose 0.21% to 99.748** as traders pared expectations for near-term rate cuts elsewhere. **Gold gained 1.40% to $4,402 an ounce**, a move consistent with investors adding safe-haven hedges even as headline risk appetite looked calm.
key_points: The **S&P 500 slipped 0.06% to 7,753**, pulling back slightly after recent record highs.
Brazil's July inflation (IPCA) cooled to **4.4% year-on-year**, down from **4.6% in June** — a three-month low.
The reading pulled inflation **back inside Brazil's central bank target range** (3%, plus or minus 1.5 points), opening the door to a **possible 25-basis-point rate cut in September**.
The **dollar index climbed 0.21% to 99.748** as traders trimmed bets on near-term rate cuts elsewhere.
**Gold jumped 1.40% to $4,402/oz** as investors leaned toward safety amid the mixed signals.

depth.background: Brazil's central bank, like most, sets an inflation target and adjusts its benchmark **Selic rate** to hit it — cutting rates to stimulate a slowing economy once inflation looks under control, and holding or raising them when prices are running hot. Brazilian inflation had spent two straight months above the top of that target band, driven largely by food prices, which kept the central bank cautious about cutting rates. Global investors watch emerging-market inflation prints like Brazil's IPCA (Índice de Preços ao Consumidor Amplo, the country's main consumer price index) closely because they shift bets on capital flows into or out of emerging-market bonds and currencies, which in turn ripple into the dollar and safe-haven assets like gold.

stories.title: Hackers used a hijacked private cellular network to sabotage a second Polish power plant
stories.what_happened: CERT Polska published a follow-up report revealing that attackers first broke into a wind farm's internet-exposed **Fortinet VPN/firewall device** — equipment meant to let remote staff securely log in. From there, they used a cellular router (a Teltonika device) to tunnel via SSH into the electricity distribution operator's **private APN** — a dedicated mobile network utilities use to remotely manage grid equipment, normally isolated from the public internet. Once inside, the attackers moved laterally into the heating plant's operational-technology network and targeted a **Wago programmable logic controller (PLC)** — the industrial computer that directly controls physical equipment. CERT Polska says the root cause was a common misconfiguration letting any device inside a private APN talk to any other device on it, meaning many other utilities — in Poland and beyond — could share the same weakness.
key_points: Poland's national cyber authority, **CERT Polska**, revealed a previously undisclosed **December 2025** attack on a heating plant serving **50,000 residents**.
Attackers pivoted through a wind farm's **VPN firewall**, then a cellular router, into the utility's **private mobile network (APN)** to reach the plant's control systems.
It's the first documented attack of its kind against European energy infrastructure — a technique never seen before.
CERT Polska says the underlying misconfiguration is **common across Poland and likely used internationally**.
The full investigation took **over three months**, which is why it wasn't in the original report on Poland's wave of energy-sector attacks.

depth.background: In late 2025, Poland's wind, solar, and heating infrastructure was hit by a wave of coordinated cyberattacks, which CERT Polska — Poland's national Computer Emergency Response Team, the government body that investigates and discloses major cyber incidents — reported on at the time. What's new today is a deep-dive follow-up on one specific incident left out of that first report because it took **three months to fully analyze**: a December 29, 2025 attack on a combined heat and power (CHP) plant supplying heating to about **50,000 people**. The attack used a genuinely novel path into the plant's industrial control systems — the computers that physically operate equipment like valves and generators — that security researchers hadn't documented before.

stories.title: Leclerc demands Ferrari investigate wild swings in race pace, as Hamilton's influence behind the scenes grows
stories.what_happened: Charles Leclerc is publicly demanding Ferrari investigate why the SF-26 has shown such wildly inconsistent race pace, saying: **'out of the last three races, there were two races where we were expecting to struggle, and we finished first and second... in the race where we expected to do well, we finished fourth and fifth.'** Separately, former F1 driver and pundit Damon Hill said Lewis Hamilton's behind-the-scenes influence has been central to Ferrari's 2026 turnaround — Hamilton reportedly sent the technical team documents describing changes he wanted, which he describes as 'ideas' rather than 'orders,' and pushed Ferrari toward the **Carbon Industrie** brake supplier he used at Mercedes. Leclerc later switched to the same Carbon Industrie brakes himself, after blaming his previous Brembo brakes for his crash at Monaco.
key_points: Charles Leclerc is demanding Ferrari **investigate its SF-26's inconsistent race pace** after wildly swinging results.
In the last three races, Ferrari finished **1st and 2nd** in two it expected to struggle in — then **4th and 5th** in one it expected to lead.
Ex-F1 driver Damon Hill says Lewis Hamilton has effectively **taken control** of Ferrari's technical direction behind the scenes.
Hamilton reportedly pushed Ferrari toward the **Carbon Industrie brake supplier** he used at Mercedes.
Leclerc later switched to the **same brakes** after blaming his old Brembo setup for his **Monaco crash**.

depth.background: Ferrari's Formula 1 team has spent years trying to close the gap to Red Bull and Mercedes, and 2026 brought a major shake-up when seven-time champion Lewis Hamilton joined the team from Mercedes, pairing with Charles Leclerc, Ferrari's long-time lead driver. Hamilton is known not just for his driving but for the deep technical influence he built at Mercedes during his championship years there, working closely with engineers on car setup and development. How much input a driver should have over engineering decisions — versus deferring entirely to the technical team — is a long-running tension in F1, especially when a superstar driver joins a team with its own established way of doing things.

stories.title: Shiprocket sets IPO price band at ₹92-97, aiming to raise ₹1,617 crore in its e-commerce logistics debut
stories.what_happened: Shiprocket has set its IPO price band at **₹92 to ₹97 per share**, valuing the **₹1,617.48 crore** issue. The IPO opens for subscription on **August 12** and closes **August 14**, with a minimum lot size of **154 shares** (about ₹14,938 for retail investors at the upper band). Shares are expected to list on the BSE and NSE around **August 19**. Shiprocket is the latest name in an already packed IPO week in India, alongside Milky Mist Dairy Food, Dhoot Transmission, Molbio Diagnostics and Behari Lal Engineering — **five mainboard IPOs** together aiming to raise over ₹7,400 crore.

IPO opens **August 12**, closes August 14; lists on BSE/NSE around **August 19**

An **IPO (initial public offering)** lets a private company sell shares to the public for the first time, raising capital and letting early investors exit.

stories.title: Colombia's earthquake death toll climbs past 160 as rescuers keep digging through rubble
stories.what_happened: The confirmed death toll rose to at least **169** people as of Tuesday morning, according to Asocapitales, an association of Colombia's capital cities, up from roughly 132 reported a day earlier. President De La Espriella said in a national briefing that **700 people were injured** and an estimated **5,000 homes** were damaged or destroyed. Rescue teams — aided by police, soldiers, volunteers, dogs and drones — worked through the night with excavators and, at times, bare hands, hunting for survivors beneath rubble in Pereira and Cali. The quake also cracked apart one tower of a historic cathedral in Manizales. Officials say the toll is expected to keep climbing as crews reach areas initially cut off by damaged roads and communications.
key_points: The death toll from Monday's **7.4-magnitude earthquake** has risen to at least **169**, per Colombia's association of capital cities.
**700 people** are injured and an estimated **5,000 homes** were damaged or destroyed, President **Abelardo De La Espriella** said.
Rescue teams are using **dogs and drones** to search for survivors trapped under collapsed buildings in **Pereira and Cali**.
The quake cracked apart a tower of a **historic cathedral** in Manizales and reduced multi-story buildings to rubble.
This is already Colombia's **deadliest earthquake in decades**, and officials expect the toll to keep climbing.

depth.background: A **7.4-magnitude earthquake** struck Colombia's coffee-growing heartland early Monday, centered near the Pacific coast and felt as far as Bogotá. It is the country's strongest quake in years, hitting a densely populated region of mid-sized cities — Pereira, Cali, Manizales — built with a mix of older masonry and modern construction, which is why the death toll and damage have been so severe. **Colombia's newly inaugurated president, Abelardo De La Espriella**, is managing his first major national disaster response just weeks into office. Search-and-rescue operations are always a race against time, since survival rates for anyone trapped under rubble fall sharply after the first 72 hours.

stories.title: Bangladesh renews pressure on India to extradite ousted PM Sheikh Hasina
stories.what_happened: Bangladesh's government told India it hopes to see the extradition process for Sheikh Hasina **expedited**, according to reporting confirmed on August 11. The message came during a courtesy meeting between India's High Commissioner to Dhaka, Dinesh Trivedi, and Bangladesh's interim leader Tarique Rahman. Bangladesh also repeated its request for India to hand over individuals accused in the killing of Osman Hadi, a case connected to the 2024 unrest. A Bangladeshi court has already convicted Hasina and her former interior minister in absentia and sentenced them to **death** for crimes against humanity linked to the deadly crackdown on protesters. India has not formally responded to the latest request.
key_points: Bangladesh again asked India to **speed up the extradition** of former PM **Sheikh Hasina**, in hiding in India since 2024.
The request came as India's High Commissioner **Dinesh Trivedi** made a courtesy call on Bangladesh's interim leader **Tarique Rahman**.
Bangladesh also renewed its demand for the return of people accused in the **killing of Osman Hadi**, tied to last year's uprising.
A Dhaka court has already **sentenced Hasina to death in absentia** for crimes against humanity over the crackdown on protesters.
India has so far given **'no comment'**, despite Bangladesh citing a **2013 bilateral extradition treaty**.

depth.background: Sheikh Hasina ruled Bangladesh for 15 years before being toppled in **August 2024** by a student-led uprising against her increasingly authoritarian government. She fled to India, where she has remained ever since, occasionally making public remarks that Dhaka says interfere in Bangladeshi politics. Bangladesh's interim government, now led by Tarique Rahman, has repeatedly demanded her return to face trial, while India — Hasina's longtime regional ally — has neither granted nor formally refused the request, leaving the issue unresolved for nearly two years.

stories.title: India's Parliament logjam deepens as Opposition demands Amit Shah explain police crackdown on NEET protesters
stories.what_happened: Congress MPs moved an **Adjournment Motion** in the Lok Sabha this week, seeking to suspend the House's scheduled business specifically to debate the police response to the **July 20 'Sansad Chalo' march**, where students protesting the NEET paper leak clashed with police at Jantar Mantar. Congress leader **Priyanka Gandhi Vadra** said the deadlock between the Opposition and government "will continue" until Home Minister **Amit Shah** personally makes a statement on the incident. Delhi Police have put the toll from that day's clash at roughly **60 injured protesters** and over **118 injured police personnel**, and contested allegations have circulated that unmarked personnel used excessive force, including against minors. Parliamentary Affairs Minister **Kiren Rijiju** said the government is "ready to discuss" the issue and that Shah will make a statement, but as of **August 11**, the standoff had already eaten into the limited sitting days left before the Monsoon Session's scheduled close on **August 13**, with both Houses repeatedly adjourning amid protests.
key_points: Congress moved an **Adjournment Motion** demanding Home Minister **Amit Shah** make a statement on police action against NEET protesters.
The protest in question: the **July 20 'Sansad Chalo' march** at Jantar Mantar, where police used **lathis and tear gas** on demonstrators.
Delhi Police say around **60 protesters** and over **118 police personnel** were injured that day.
With only a few sitting days left in the **Monsoon Session**, bills on women's reservation, delimitation and the **FCRA** law are stuck behind the standoff.
Parliamentary Affairs Minister **Kiren Rijiju** says the government is ready to let Shah address the House.

depth.background: On **July 20**, thousands of students and youth groups marched on Parliament to protest alleged irregularities and a leak in the **NEET** medical-entrance exam, demanding the education minister's resignation. When protesters pushed past barricades, police responded with lathi charges and tear gas, and both sides accuse the other of provoking the clash, with allegations that some students, including minors, were hurt. The Opposition **INDIA bloc** has used the incident to repeatedly disrupt Parliament's ongoing Monsoon Session, insisting Home Minister Amit Shah personally answer for the police response before other business proceeds — a separate but related flashpoint to this week's Jharkhand exam-protest clash, which is fuelling the same broader standoff.

stories.title: India approves trial run of 1 billion plastic ₹10 and ₹20 notes
stories.what_happened: The Indian government has cleared a plan to print **1 billion polymer banknotes** each in the **₹10 and ₹20** denominations for field trials, Finance Minister **Nirmala Sitharaman** told the Rajya Sabha in a written reply on **August 11**. She said the **Reserve Bank of India** put forward the proposal after its central board recommended testing polymer notes based on how other countries have used them. If the trials go well, polymer notes could later be issued regularly in these denominations, running alongside the existing paper ₹10 and ₹20 notes rather than replacing them immediately. Sitharaman said the procurement process is still at an early stage, so the government cannot yet estimate a launch timeline or the total cost of the switch.
key_points: The government approved printing **1 billion polymer banknotes** each of **₹10 and ₹20** for field trials, Parliament was told.
Finance Minister **Nirmala Sitharaman** confirmed the move in a written reply to the **Rajya Sabha** on **August 11**.
The **RBI's central board** recommended the switch after studying how other countries use polymer notes.
Polymer notes will circulate **alongside** existing paper notes, not replace them outright.
The government says it's **too early** to estimate a launch date or cost, since procurement hasn't started.

depth.background: India currently prints all its currency on cotton-based paper, which wears out faster, is easier to counterfeit and is more vulnerable to moisture than **polymer (plastic) banknotes**, already used for decades by countries like Australia, the UK, Canada and Singapore. The RBI has floated polymer notes before, including a small ₹10 field trial roughly a decade ago in a handful of cities, but never scaled it nationally. Polymer notes typically cost more to produce upfront but last several times longer than paper notes, which can lower costs over their full lifespan and cut down on how often notes need reprinting.

stories.title: Jharkhand exam protest escalates into a Parliament clash after police use water cannons on job aspirants
stories.what_happened: Police in Jharkhand used **water cannons, tear gas and lathi charges** against job aspirants protesting near the state Assembly, in a clash that escalated a recruitment-exam dispute already running for more than two weeks. In response, ruling NDA MPs staged a protest inside Parliament in Delhi on **August 11**, marching from the Parliament Library to the main gate ('Makar Dwar') chanting slogans like 'Rahul Gandhi Jawab Do' ('Rahul Gandhi, answer'). The BJP accused Gandhi of being **'either culpable or incapable'** of acting against the Jharkhand government, and said he was avoiding a parliamentary debate on the student protests. Opposition INDIA-bloc MPs confronted the NDA MPs at Parliament's gate, with security personnel forming a cordon to keep the two groups apart.
key_points: Police used **water cannons, tear gas and lathi-charges** on job aspirants protesting near the Jharkhand Assembly.
The protest is over alleged **irregularities in recruitment exams**, an issue simmering for over two weeks.
Ruling **NDA MPs marched inside Parliament**, chanting slogans demanding Congress leader **Rahul Gandhi** answer for the crackdown.
Jharkhand is run by a Congress-JMM-RJD coalition, which the BJP says is either **'culpable or incapable'** on the issue.
**Opposition INDIA bloc MPs faced off** with NDA MPs at Parliament's main gate, with security forming a cordon between them.

depth.background: This story began when Jharkhand's government agreed to cancel a competitive recruitment exam after mass cheating allegations, but the affected job aspirants kept protesting for over two weeks, saying cancellation alone didn't fix the underlying unfairness in the hiring process. Jharkhand is governed by an opposition INDIA-bloc coalition (Congress, JMM and RJD), which put the state government under the national opposition's political umbrella. That set up a clash with the ruling BJP-led NDA in Delhi, which has used the protests to target Congress leader Rahul Gandhi directly.
